record.title: Conjecture on the imaginary zeros and separation of Stirling permutation polynomials
record.statement:
Let $T_n(x)$ be the polynomial defined by the exponential generating function

$$
T(x,z)=\sum_{n=0}^\infty T_n(x)\frac{z^n}{n!}.
$$

For polynomials with only real coefficients and only imaginary zeros, say that $f(x)$ **separates** $F(x)$ if $\deg F=\deg f+2$ and the ordered real and imaginary parts of the zeros of $f(x)$ separately interlace those of $F(x)$. **Imaginary-zero and separation conjecture.** For $n\geq 2$, all zeros of $T_n(x)/x$ are imaginary and $T_n(x)/x$ separates $T_{n+1}(x)/x$. This conjecture predicts a real-root-analogue property for the polynomials $T_n(x)$, extending the known real-zero and separation properties of the related polynomials $R_n(x)$.
record.source_name: Shi-Mei Ma and Hai-Na Wang, “Enumeration of a dual set of Stirling permutations by their alternating runs”, arXiv:1506.08716 (2015).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1506.08716

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2015).

record.title: Non-embeddability conjecture for cube-connected cycles
record.statement:
Let $CCC_n$ be the cubic cube-connected-cycles graph obtained by replacing every vertex of the $n$-cube by an $n$-cycle. For $n=3$ its diameter is $6$, and for $n\geq4$ its diameter is $\left\lfloor\frac{5n-4}{2}\right\rfloor$.

**Cube-connected-cycles non-embeddability conjecture.** For the tested values $n=3,4,5$, $CCC_n$ is not $(n+1)$-tr.embeddable.

This is a computationally supported conjecture about the existence of restricted hypercube embeddings for the standard cube-connected-cycles family; no general proof or resolution is given in the source.

record.title: Existence of a primitive ergodic element in a treeable equivalence relation
record.statement:
Let ${\mathcal{R}}$ be an ergodic treeable equivalence relation of cost $>1$, and let $[\mathcal{R}]$ denote its full group. A subequivalence relation of ${\mathcal{R}}$ is **primitive** if it admits a treeing that extends to a treeing of ${\mathcal{R}}$. 

**Primitive-element conjecture.** There exists an ergodic element $f \in [\mathcal{R}]$ such that the subequivalence relation generated by $f$ is primitive in ${\mathcal{R}}$.

Such an element would provide a primitive ergodic subequivalence relation generated by a single transformation, complementing the paper's results on surjections from treeable equivalence relations. The supplied context does not state whether this conjecture has been resolved.
record.source_name: Lewis Bowen, “Simple and large equivalence relations”, arXiv:1507.04841 (2015).

record.title: Permanent-cycle conjecture for $a_{\sigma_n}u_{\rho_n-\sigma_n}$
record.statement:
Let $C_{2^n}$ be the cyclic group of order $2^n$, and let $a_{\sigma_n}$ and $u_{\rho_n-\sigma_n}$ denote the Euler and orientation classes associated to the representations $\sigma_n$ and $\rho_n-\sigma_n$. Consider the slice spectral sequence for $C_{2^n}$. **Permanent-cycle conjecture.** The element

$$
a_{\sigma_n}u_{\rho_n-\sigma_n}
$$

is a permanent cycle in the slice spectral sequence for $C_{2^n}$. Computational evidence supports this for $n=3$, but the authors note that the conjecture may be too strong: for larger $n$, differentials could occur, possibly reflecting Adams differentials.
record.source_name: Michael A. Hill, “On the fate of η^3 in higher analogues of Real bordism”, arXiv:1507.08083 (2015).

record.title: Compressed zero-divisor graph description for ideals in UFDs
record.statement:
Let $D$ be a unique factorization domain and let $I$ be an ideal with a minimal expression

$$
I=\bigcup_{\alpha\in\Lambda}\left\langle\prod_{k=1}^{Q_\alpha}p_{\alpha_k}^{s_{\alpha_k}}\right\rangle.
$$

Let $\"]\phi:D\to D/I$ be the canonical map, and let $\"]\mathfrak B$ be the zero-divisor basis of $D/I$, consisting of suitable nonassociate divisors of the generators. The compressed zero-divisor graph has vertices represented by annihilator-equivalence classes of elements $\"]\phi(\prod_i d_i)$ with each $d_i\in\mathfrak B$.

**Compressed-graph structure conjecture.** An edge joins the vertices represented by $\"]\phi(\prod_i d_i)$ and $\"]\phi(\prod_i b_i)$ if and only if

$$
n_\alpha\mid\prod_i d_i b_i
$$

for some $\"]\alpha\in\Lambda$.
record.source_name: Rachael Alvir, “Zero-Divisor Graphs of Quotient Rings”, arXiv:1508.02432 (2015).

record.title: Basis conjecture for the functions associated with two-step equivalence classes
record.statement:
For $k=0,1,2$, let $\{f^{(k)}\}$ be the set of functions realized as

$$
\sum_{T\in\mathcal{C}}F_{\operatorname{ID}(T)},
$$

where $\mathcal{C}$ is a single equivalence class of $\equiv^k$. **Basis conjecture.** The set $\{f^{(2)}\}$ forms a basis for the quasisymmetric functions. This concerns the generating functions associated with the equivalence classes introduced in the paper; the supplied text does not indicate whether the assertion has been proved or remains open.

record.title: Bordeaux Conjecture on 3-coloring planar graphs
record.statement: Let $G$ be a planar graph. Two cycles are **intersecting** if they have at least one common vertex. **Bordeaux Conjecture.** Every planar graph without intersecting $3$-cycles and without $5$-cycles is $3$-colorable. This conjecture is one of the two Borodin–Raspaud relaxations related to planar $3$-coloring. The source gives no resolution and proceeds to discuss the stronger condition involving adjacent, rather than intersecting, triangles.

record.title: Subdivision conjecture for strictly convex vertex and edge-midpoint drawings
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, and let **subdivision** mean a graph obtained by replacing edges by paths, possibly subdividing edges more than once. Let $\mathcal{G}_s^s$ denote the class of graphs admitting a straight-line drawing whose vertices and edge midpoints are both strictly convex.

**Subdivision conjecture.** Every graph has a subdivision obtained by multiplying subdividing its edges such that the resulting graph belongs to $\mathcal{G}_s^s$.

The conjecture is motivated by examples in which subdivisions of $K_{2,n}$ and $K_{3,3}$ admit such drawings even though the original graphs do not. The supplied text gives no resolution.
record.source_name: Ignacio García-Marco and Kolja Knauer, “Drawing graphs with vertices and edges in convex position”, arXiv:1509.01981 (2016).

record.title: Finiteness conjecture for permutation binomials over quadratic finite fields
record.statement:
Let $q$ be a prime power, let $\Bbb F_{q^2}$ be the finite field with $q^2$ elements, and let $r>2$ be a fixed prime. For $a\in\Bbb F_{q^2}^*$, define

$$
f=a{\tt X}+{\tt X}^{r(q-1)+1}.
$$

A polynomial is a **permutation polynomial** of $\Bbb F_{q^2}$ if it induces a permutation of that field. **Finiteness conjecture.** Under the assumption $a^{q+1}\ne 1$, there are only finitely many pairs $(q,a)$ for which $f$ is a permutation polynomial of $\Bbb F_{q^2}$. This conjecture is motivated by results for $r=3,5,7$, where the corresponding pairs $(q,a)$ with $a^{q+1}\ne 1$ are known to be finite; the general case for fixed prime $r>2$ remains open.
record.source_name: Xiang-dong Hou, “Permutation Polynomials of F_q^2 of the form aX+X^r(q-1)+1”, arXiv:1510.00437 (2015).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1510.00437

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2015).

record.title: Albert and Bousquet-Mélou's $(x+1)$-positivity conjecture for balanced path projections
record.statement: Let $\mathcal{V}$ be a positive vertical path with $u$ up-steps and $d$ down-steps, let $Q$ be the set of quarter-planar paths with $r$ right-steps, $l$ left-steps, and vertical projection $\mathcal{V}$, and let $G_1$ be the peak-count generating function over $Q$. A polynomial is **$(x+1)$-positive** when it belongs to $\mathbb{N}_0[x+1]$. **Albert and Bousquet-Mélou's conjecture.** If $a=b$ and $c=d$, then $G_1$ is $(x+1)$-positive. The statement is presented as Albert and Bousquet-Mélou's Conjecture (P2), and the paper says that it implies their quarter-planar-loop conjecture; the balanced parameters and the roles of $a,b,c,d$ should be checked against the paper's earlier definitions.

record.title: Higher-dimensional Borg uniqueness conjecture for periodic Schrödinger operators
record.statement:
Let $H=-\Delta+V(x)$ be a periodic Schrödinger operator, with dispersion relation consisting of the pairs $(k,\lambda)$ for which $H(k)$ has a non-zero solution at energy $\lambda$. An **entire dispersion branch** is an entire function $f(k)$ whose graph $\lambda=f(k)$ lies in the dispersion relation.

**Higher-dimensional Borg conjecture.** The following claims are equivalent:
1. The potential $V$ is constant.
2. There exists an entire function whose graph $\lambda=f(k)$ belongs to the dispersion relation.

This is proposed as the higher-dimensional analogue of Borg's uniqueness theorem for the one-dimensional Hill operator. The source explicitly says that the equivalence probably still holds and gives no resolution; the two-dimensional version is not the statement extracted here.
record.source_name: Peter Kuchment, “An overview of periodic elliptic operators”, arXiv:1510.00971 (2016).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1510.00971

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of October 2015). “In $2D$, the conjecture was proven by Kn\"orrer and Trubowitz .”

record.title: Harmse–Remmel conjecture on c-Wilf and strong c-Wilf equivalence
record.statement:
Let $P,Q
\in\mathcal F_{n,k}$, where $
\mathcal F_{n,k}$ denotes the relevant family of generalized Euler permutations. They are **c-Wilf equivalent** when $A_P(0,t)=A_Q(0,t)$, and **strongly c-Wilf equivalent** when $A_P(x,t)=A_Q(x,t)$, where

$$
A_P(x,t)=\sum_{n\geq0}\frac{t^n}{(kn)!}\sum_{F\in\mathcal F_{n,k}}x^{P\text{-mch}(F)}.
$$

**Harmse–Remmel conjecture.** $P$ and $Q$ are c-Wilf equivalent if and only if they are strongly c-Wilf equivalent. The conjecture extends Nakamura's $k=1$ formulation to $k\geq2$; the source does not state whether it has been resolved.
record.source_name: Ran Pan and Jeffrey B. Remmel, “Asymptotics for minimal overlapping patterns for generalized Euler permutations, standard tableaux of rectangular shape, and column strict arrays”, arXiv:1510.08190 (2016).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1510.08190

record.title: Linear coloring conjecture for touching sets of strings
record.statement: A **touching set of strings** is a finite family of strings in the plane in which no pair crosses, and it is **$k$-touching** if every point of the plane belongs to at most $k$ strings. **Linear coloring conjecture.** There is a constant $c>0$ such that every $k$-touching set of strings can be colored with $ck$ colors. The conjecture was subsequently proved by Fox and Pach, who obtained the bound $6ek+1$ colors.
record.source_name: Louis Esperet, Daniel Gonçalves and Arnaud Labourel, “Coloring non-crossing strings”, arXiv:1511.03827 (2016).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1511.03827

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of November 2015); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “solved”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

record.title: Additive coloring conjecture for 1-intersecting touching strings
record.statement: A **1-intersecting set of strings** is a set of strings in which any two strings intersect in at most one point, and it is **$k$-touching** if every point of the plane belongs to at most $k$ strings. **Additive coloring conjecture.** There is a constant $c>0$ such that every $k$-touching set of 1-intersecting strings can be colored with $k+c$ colors. No resolution is supplied in the source excerpt.

record.title: The non-overlapping solitons conjecture
record.statement: Let $p$ be a prime and let $g_1,g_2\geq 2$. For each $g$, let $\mathfrak S(p,g)$ be the connected collection of cells that starts at $p^g$ and contains only powers of $p$ larger than two. These collections are called $Z$-solitons. **Non-overlapping solitons conjecture.** Two distinct solitons $\mathfrak S(p,g_1)$ and $\mathfrak S(p,g_2)$ neither overlap nor touch each other. The conjecture is verified for $p=2$ by the complete description of the solitons in that case; it remains open for odd primes, whose solitons have a more complicated structure.
record.source_name: Cristian Cobeli, Mihai Prunescu and Alexandru Zaharescu, “A growth model based on the arithmetic Z-game”, arXiv:1511.04315 (2015).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1511.04315

record.title: The multiplicative Gilbreath conjecture for the left edge
record.statement: Let $T_{\mathbb N^*}$ be the infinite triangle generated by iterating the $Z$-rule on the positive integers, and call its first column the left edge. A number is **square-free** when no square of a prime divides it. **Multiplicative Gilbreath conjecture.** Every number on the left edge of $T_{\mathbb N^*}$ is square-free; equivalently, the maximal power of any prime occurring in the prime factorization of a left-edge entry is one. This is the multiplicative analogue of the Gilbreath conjecture and is supported by computer evidence; the source notes that it is proved for the solitons $\mathfrak S(2,g)$, but does not establish the assertion for the entire left edge.
record.source_name: Cristian Cobeli, Mihai Prunescu and Alexandru Zaharescu, “A growth model based on the arithmetic Z-game”, arXiv:1511.04315 (2015).

record.title: Finite obstruction conjecture for semiacyclic tournaments
record.statement:
A **tournament** is a complete oriented graph, and a tournament is **semiacyclic** if it admits a numbering of its vertices with no directed cycle having positive winding number. A tournament is **minimally not semiacyclic** if it is not semiacyclic, but deleting any vertex leaves a tournament whose vertices can be numbered so that it is semiacyclic.

**Finite obstruction conjecture.** There is a finite list of tournaments that are minimally not semiacyclic.

This asks for a finite obstruction set when the vertex numbering may be chosen freely, in contrast with the obstruction list for a fixed numbering given by Postnikov and Stanley. The source provides no resolution, so the conjecture remains open.
record.source_name: Gábor Hetyei, “Efron's coins and the Linial arrangement”, arXiv:1511.04482 (2016).
record.references:

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2015).

record.title: Finite obstruction conjecture for dominance graphs of coin systems
record.statement:
A **dominance graph of a system of coins** is the tournament associated with the pairwise dominance relations among the coins. Such a tournament is **minimally not a dominance graph of a system of coins** if it is not the dominance graph of any system of coins, but deleting any vertex yields the dominance graph of a system of coins.

**Finite obstruction conjecture.** There is a finite list of tournaments that are minimally not dominance graphs of systems of coins.

This is the analogous finite-obstruction question for dominance graphs of coin systems. The source provides no resolution, so the conjecture remains open.

record.title: Polynomial enumeration conjecture for non-occupied corners in symmetric tree-like tableaux
record.statement:
Let $n$ be an integer, let $\mathcal T^{sym}_{2n+1}$ be the set of symmetric tree-like tableaux of size $2n+1$, let $noc(T)$ denote the number of non-occupied corners of $T$, and define $left^*(T)=left(T)-1$. Let

$$
T_{2n-3}^{sym}(x)
$$

denote the corresponding $x$-analogue of the enumeration of symmetric tree-like tableaux. The **$x$-analogue of the enumeration of non-occupied corners** is the weighted sum of $noc(T)$ with weight $x^{left^*(T)}$.

**Symmetric polynomial enumeration conjecture.**

$$
\sum_{T\in\mathcal T^{sym}_{2n+1}}noc(T)x^{left^*(T)}=\left[2nx^2+2(2n^2-4n+1)x+\frac{(n-2)(n-1)(4n-3)}{3}\right]\cdot T_{2n-3}^{sym}(x).
$$

The expression is presented as the result of computer exploration, and the supplied text does not state a proof or resolution.
record.source_name: Alice L. L. Gao, Emily X. L. Gao, Patxi Laborde-Zubieta and Brian Y. Sun, “Enumeration of Corners in Tree-like Tableaux”, arXiv:1511.05456 (2016).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1511.05456

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of November 2015). “The second conjecture is proven in the same way, which also gives us the enumeration of corners in type $B$ permutation tableaux, in symmetric alternative tableaux (Theorem ).”

record.title: No exponentially convergent spectral-ratio families in the P≤ cases
record.statement: Let $h$ be a pseudo-Anosov mapping class and let $\operatorname{\omega}(h)$ denote its spectral ratio. For a surface and an infinite family of pseudo-Anosov mapping classes, a P$_{\leq}$ case means that $\operatorname{\omega}(h)\leq 1+1/\operatorname{poly}(|h|)$, while an E case means that $\operatorname{\omega}(h)\leq 1+1/\exp(|h|)$. **P$_{\leq}$ versus E conjecture.** In all P$_{\leq}$ cases, there is no family of pseudo-Anosov mapping classes whose spectral ratios converge to one exponentially; equivalently, none of the P$_{\leq}$ cases are E cases. The claim distinguishes polynomially slow convergence of the spectral ratio from exponential convergence in the surface-by-surface classification. The supplied text gives no resolution, so the assertion remains open.
